Snapshot works. Open http://maker:4001/snapshot.html — the **"CSS Grid"** item already has a preserved copy (green **"📄 Copy saved"** badge); others don't yet.

**Please try:**
1. **View a preserved copy.** On the "CSS Grid" item, click **📄 View copy**. → An overlay opens showing the **saved, read-only version of the page** — its text is kept so you could still read it even if the original vanished. Close it with × or by clicking outside.
2. **Preserve a page yourself.** On another item, click **📄 Save a copy**. After a moment it shows "Saving a copy…" then gains the **green badge** and now offers **View copy** and **↻ Update copy**.

Now the decisions that shape this feature — I built it one way but want your call:

- **When should a copy be made?** Right now it's **manual** — you click "Save a copy" on the ones you care about. The alternatives are: **automatically preserve a copy of every bookmark** when you save it, or a **default that you can turn on/off** (auto for everything, but still manual control per item). Which fits how you'd use this? (Auto keeps everything safe but stores far more; manual keeps it lightweight and deliberate.)

- **What should the copy preserve?** I simulated a **readable text version** of the page (the words/article, stripped of clutter). The alternative is trying to keep the **full visual page** (layout and images as it looked). For guarding against link rot, which matters more to you — the readable content, or the exact appearance?

- And is a **read-only saved copy plus an "Update copy" option** (to re-capture if the page changed) the right level of control?
